chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Salamah al-Lu'lu'i, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Shall I not inform you of how the Islam of Salman and Abu Dharr was?
So the man said, and he was hasty: 'As for the Islam of Salman, I have known it. Inform me of the Islam of Abu Dharr.'

He said: 'Indeed, Abu Dharr was in the valley of Mar, tending his sheep. A wolf came from the right of his sheep, so he struck the wolf with his staff. The wolf came from his left, so Abu Dharr struck it.'
Then Abu Dharr said to it, 'I have not seen a wolf more vicious than you, nor more evil.' The wolf said to him, 'More evil than I, by Allah, are the people of Mecca.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a Prophet to them, but they belied him and insulted him.' This fell into the ears of Abu Dharr.
So he said to his wife, 'Bring me my provisions, my bag, and my staff.' Then he set out on foot, intending Mecca, to know the news of the wolf and what it had brought him.
Until he reached Mecca and entered it in a hot hour, having grown weary and exhausted. He came to Zamzam, being thirsty, so he scooped a bucket and it turned out to be milk.
So he said to himself, 'This, by Allah, indicates to me that what the wolf informed me of and what I have come for is true.' So he drank and came to a side of the Masjid.
There was a circle of Quraysh, so he sat with them. He saw them insulting the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), just as the wolf had said.
They did not cease in that, mentioning the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and insulting him, until Abu Talib came from the end of the day.
When they saw him, some of them said to others, 'Refrain, for his uncle has come.' So they refrained. He did not cease talking to them and speaking to them until it was the end of the day.
Then he stood up, and I rose following him. He turned to me and said, 'Mention your need.' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what do you do with him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'And you will do that?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Come tomorrow at this time to me, until I take you to him.'
He said: 'I spent that night in the Masjid. When it was the next day, I sat with them. They did not cease mentioning the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and insulting him.'
Until Abu Talib appeared. When they saw him, some said to others, 'Hold back, for his uncle has come.' So they held back.
He did not cease talking to them until he stood up, so I followed him. I greeted him, so he said, 'Mention your need.'

I said, 'The Prophet sent among you.' He said, 'And what do you do with him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'And you will do that?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Rise with me.' So I followed him, and he took me to a house in which was Hamza (peace be upon him).
I greeted him and sat down. He said to me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'I testified.'
So Hamza took me to a house in which was Ja'far (peace be upon him). I greeted him and sat down.
Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger?' I said, 'I testified.'
He took me to a house in which was Ali (peace be upon him). I greeted him and sat down.
He said, 'What is your need?' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'I testified.'
He took me to a house in which was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I greeted him and sat down.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'The Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'

He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'I testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me, 'O Abu Dharr! Go to your land, for you will find a cousin of yours who has died and has no heir except you. So take his wealth and stay with your family until our matter becomes apparent.'
So Abu Dharr returned, took the wealth, and stayed with his family until the matter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became apparent.
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is the hadith of Abu Dharr and his Islam, may Allah be pleased with him.'
And as for the hadith of Salman, you have heard it.
He said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, narrate to me the hadith of Salman.'
'You have heard it.' And he did not narrate it to him due to his bad manners.

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abu Dharr (a companion of the Prophet)
key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: Our matter (the public proclamation of Islam)

ai.seo_question: How did Abu Dharr al-Ghari convert to Islam according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique, miraculous nature of Abu Dharr’s early faith, where a speaking wolf serves as a divine sign prompting his journey to Mecca. It illustrates the gradual public revelation of Islam, as the Prophet instructs him to remain in his tribe until the 'matter becomes manifest,' reflecting the strategic patience of the early Meccan period. The narrative also subtly underscores the high scholarly etiquette, noting that Salman al-Farsi was excluded from hearing this specific account due to his brevity in transmission.

en.hubeali: H 14905 – Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbaar, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Salmat Al-Lului, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘Shall Iasws not inform you of how Salmanar and Abu Dharrar (brought Islam)?’ So a man interrupted hastily and said, ‘As for the Islam of Salmanar, so I have understood it. Inform me of the Islam of Abu Dharrar’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> was in the middle of tending his<sup>ar</sup> sheep when he<sup>ar</sup> saw a wolf passing by on the right of his<sup>ar</sup> sheep. So he<sup>ar</sup> chased the wolf away by his<sup>ar</sup> staff. So the wolf came from his<sup>ar</sup> right.

So Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> chased it away. Then Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> said to it, ‘I<sup>ar</sup> have not seen a wolf more vicious or evil than you’. So the wolf said to him<sup>ar</sup>, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The people of Makkah are more evil than I am.

Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Sent a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> to them, so they belied him<sup>saww</sup> and insulted him<sup>saww</sup>’. This reverberated in the ears of Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup>.

So he<sup>ar</sup> said to his<sup>ar</sup> wife, ‘Prepare my<sup>ar</sup> provisions and give it to me<sup>asws</sup> along with my<sup>asws</sup> walking stick’. Then he<sup>ar</sup> went out on his feet towards Makkah to know the news of what the wolf had come up with.

He<sup>ar</sup> reached Makkah and entered it at a time when it was hot, and he<sup>ar</sup> was exhausted. So he<sup>ar</sup> came up to Zamzam (well) and was thirsty. He<sup>ar</sup> filled a bucket and it turned out to be milk.

So he<sup>ar</sup> said to himself, ‘This evidences to me<sup>ar</sup> to what the wolf had informed me<sup>ar</sup> of and what I<sup>ar</sup> have come to is right. So he<sup>ar</sup> drank and went to a side from the sides of the Masjid.
There was a group of Qureysh there, so he<sup>ar</sup> sat among them. He<sup>ar</sup> saw them insulting the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> just as the wolf had said.
They did not stop mentioning the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and insulting him<sup>saww</sup> until Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> came up at the end of the night.

So when they saw him<sup>as</sup>, some of them said to the others, ‘Refrain, for his<sup>saww</sup> uncle<sup>as</sup> is coming!’ They refrained. He<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘He<sup>as</sup> did not stop narrating to them and speaking to them until it was the end of the day.

Then he<sup>as</sup> stood up, and I<sup>ar</sup> arose following his<sup>as</sup> footsteps. So he<sup>as</sup> turned towards me<sup>ar</sup> and said, ‘Mention your<sup>ar</sup> need’. So I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘This Prophet<sup>saww</sup> who has been Sent among you’.

He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘And what do you want to do with him<sup>saww</sup>?’ I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘Believe with him<sup>saww</sup>, and ratify him<sup>saww</sup> and present myself<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> will not command me<sup>ar</sup> for anything except that I<sup>ar</sup> shall obey him<sup>saww</sup>’. He<sup>as</sup> said, ‘And you<sup>ar</sup> will do it?’ I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘Yes’.
So he<sup>as</sup> said, ‘Come to me<sup>as</sup> tomorrow at this time and I<sup>as</sup> will take you<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>’.
I<sup>ar</sup> waited in the Masjid that night until when it was the morning, I<sup>ar</sup> sat with them (Qureysh).

They did not stop mentioning the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and insulting him<sup>saww</sup> until Abu Talib<sup>as</sup> came over. So when they saw him<sup>as</sup>, some of them said to the others, ‘Withhold yourselves, for his<sup>saww</sup> uncle<sup>as</sup> has come’. So they withheld.

He<sup>as</sup> did not stop narrating to them until he<sup>as</sup> stood up from them. So I<sup>ar</sup> followed him<sup>as</sup>. I<sup>ar</sup> greeted him<sup>as</sup>, so he<sup>as</sup> said, ‘State your<sup>ar</sup> need’.

So I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, the one Sent among you’. He<sup>as</sup> said, ‘And what will you do with him<sup>saww</sup>?’ So I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘Believe with him<sup>saww</sup>, and ratify him<sup>saww</sup>, and present myself<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>, and there is nothing that he<sup>saww</sup> will command me<sup>ar</sup> for, but that I<sup>ar</sup> will obey him<sup>saww</sup>’. He<sup>as</sup> said, ‘And you<sup>ar</sup> will do it’. I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘Yes’. 
He<sup>as</sup> said, ‘Come with me<sup>as</sup>.
So I<sup>ar</sup> followed him<sup>as</sup>. He<sup>as</sup> took me<sup>ar</sup> to a house in which was Hamza<sup>as</sup>.

So I<sup>ar</sup> greeted him<sup>as</sup> and sat down. He<sup>as</sup> said to me<sup>ar</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>ar</sup> need?’ I said, ‘This Prophet<sup>saww</sup> Sent among you’. So he<sup>as</sup> said, ‘So what is your<sup>ar</sup> need to him<sup>saww</sup>?’

I said, ‘Believe with him<sup>saww</sup>, and ratify him<sup>saww</sup>, and present myself<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> will not command me for anything but that I<sup>ar</sup> will obey him<sup>saww</sup>’.

So he<sup>as</sup> said, ‘Do you testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘I<sup>ar</sup> testify’.
So Hamza<sup>as</sup> took me<sup>ar</sup> to a house in which was Ja’far<sup>as</sup>. I<sup>ar</sup> greeted him<sup>as</sup>, and sat down.

Ja’far<sup>as</sup> said to me, ‘What is your<sup>ar</sup> need?’ So I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘This Prophet<sup>saww</sup> Sent among you’. He<sup>as</sup> said, ‘And what is your<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>?’

So I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘Believe with him<sup>saww</sup>, and ratify him<sup>saww</sup>, and present myself<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> will not command me<sup>ar</sup> for anything but that I<sup>ar</sup> will obey him<sup>saww</sup>’.

So he<sup>as</sup> said, ‘Do you<sup>ar</sup> testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, One with no associates to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is His<sup>azwj</sup> servant and His<sup>azwj</sup> Messenger<sup>saww</sup>?’ I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘I<sup>ar</sup> testify’.
So he<sup>as</sup> took me to a house in which was Ali<sup>asws</sup>. I<sup>ar</sup> greeted him<sup>asws</sup> and sat down.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘What is your need?’ I said, ‘This Prophet<sup>saww</sup> Sent among you’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is your<sup>ar</sup> need to him<sup>saww</sup>?’ I said, ‘Believe with him<sup>saww</sup>, and ratify him<sup>saww</sup>, and present myself<sup>ar</sup> to him<sup>saww</sup>, and there is nothing that he<sup>saww</sup> will command me<sup>ar</sup> for but I<sup>ar</sup> will obey him<sup>saww</sup>’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Do you<sup>ar</sup> testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is His<sup>azwj</sup> Messenger<sup>saww</sup>?’ I said, ‘I<sup>ar</sup> testify’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> took me<sup>ar</sup> to a house in which was the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So I<sup>ar</sup> greeted and sat down.
So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to me<sup>ar</sup>: ‘What is your<sup>ar</sup> need?’ I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> Sent among you’.

He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And what is your<sup>ar</sup> need to him<sup>saww</sup>?’ I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘Believe in him<sup>saww</sup>, and ratify him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> will not command me<sup>ar</sup> for anything but that I<sup>ar</sup> will obey him<sup>saww</sup>’.

So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do you<sup>ar</sup> testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So I<sup>ar</sup> said, ‘I<sup>ar</sup> testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.

So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to me<sup>ar</sup>; ‘O Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup>! Go to your city, for you<sup>ar</sup> will find that a son of your<sup>ar</sup> uncle has died and there is no inheritor for him apart from you<sup>ar</sup>. So take his wealth and stay in the presence of your<sup>ar</sup> family until our<sup>saww</sup> matter is made apparent’.
So Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> returned, took the wealth and stayed in the presence of his family until the matter of the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> was made apparent’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘This is the Hadith of Abu Dharr<sup>ar</sup> and his<sup>ar</sup> Islam, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with him<sup>ar</sup>.
And as for the Hadith of Salman<sup>ar</sup>, so you have heard it’.
So the man said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, narrate to me the Hadith of Salman<sup>ar</sup>’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘You have heard it’. (The narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> did not narrate it due to his bad manners’.
en.sarwar: 458. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abaan Bin Usmaan, from Zurara, who has narrated the following:
‘Samama Bin Asaal was captured by the cavalry of the Prophet (saww) and the Rasool Allah (saww) had said; ‘Our Allah (azwj)! Make me (saww) to overcome Samama!’
So the Rasool Allah (saww) said to him: ‘I (saww) give you one of three choices. I (saww) could kill you’.
He said, ‘Then you (saww) would have killed a great person’.
He said, ‘Then you (saww) would find me to be expensive’.
He (saww) said: ‘Or I (saww) give safety to you’.
He said, ‘Then you would find me to be thankful’.
He (saww) said: ‘So I (saww) give safety to you’.

He said, ‘I hereby testify that there is no god except Allah (azwj), and you (saww) Muhammad (saww) are the Rasool Allah (saww), and by Allah (azwj), I knew you (saww) were the Rasool Allah (saww) when I saw you (saww), and I did not testify by it whilst I was in bondage’.
